**Research Experience:**
While both applicants have some research experience, APP-0002's experience appears to be more extensive. [E4] mentions that APP-0002 worked on a capstone project titled "Software Architecture approaches to optimize plug-and-play content", which suggests that they have engaged in research-related activities. Additionally, [E1] and [E3] highlight their ability to learn new technologies quickly and function effectively under real project constraints.

In contrast, APP-0008's research experience is not as clearly documented. While [E7] mentions that APP-0008 showed genuine potential, but had inconsistent performance across courses, there is no explicit mention of a formal research position or publication in a peer-reviewed journal.

**Recommendations:**
Both applicants have received strong recommendations from their supervisors. However, [E1] and [E3] from APP-0002's supervisor highlight their ability to learn new technologies quickly and function effectively under real project constraints, which suggests that they are well-prepared for the challenge of the INFOTECH program.

In contrast, [E7] from APP-0008's supervisor mentions that their performance across courses was at times inconsistent, but also highlights their potential. However, [E2] does not explicitly mention any weaknesses or areas for improvement in APP-0008's work experience.

**Program Intended Specialization:**
APP-0002 has expressed interest in Computer Hardware/Software Engineering, while APP-0008 has expressed interest in Communications.

**English Proficiency:**
Both applicants have taken the TOEFL iBT exam and achieved satisfactory scores. However, APP-0002's score (112) is higher than APP-0008's score (86).

In summary, while both applicants have some research experience and strong recommendations, APP-0002 appears to have more extensive research experience and a stronger academic record. APP-0008, on the other hand, has shown potential but had inconsistent performance across courses.
